verdict.rationale: Cactus lets you build task-specialized tool-calling models rather than configurable assistant personas. You submit your tools, a product description and example messages to generate training data (POST /generations, /tool_schemas), fine-tune Needle 3 on the platform or with local LoRA, then download the model. You can also declare custom tools by decorating functions. This delivers specialization through a developer fine-tuning workflow, not a simple assistant-configuration feature. Hands-on reports suggest results are weak unless the use case is matched exactly, and that the model struggles beyond about 10 tools. missing for 10: a first-class assistant or persona configuration feature (system prompts, saved task profiles), documentation framing this as building assistants, and independent evidence that fine-tuned specialized models perform reliably.
